title: Shape Enum
story: You're building a geometry calculator. Circles need radius, rectangles need width and height, triangles need base and height — but they all share one thing: you can compute their area!
why: The Shape enum shows how different variants can carry different numbers of fields, yet one function can handle them all with match.
analogy: The Shape enum is like a toolbox — you pull out the circle tool for circles, the rectangle tool for rectangles. Same toolbox, different tools for different jobs.
try_it: Add a `Square(side: Float64)` variant. Its area is `side * side`. Update `area` and `describe`, then test with all four shapes.
tips: Different variants can have different numbers of payload fields — Circle has 1, Rectangle has 2
Use `3.14159` or `3.14` for pi — there's no built-in pi constant at this level
Match arms receive all payload fields: `Rectangle(width, height)` grabs both values
common_mistakes: Using `Circle(r)` then `Rectangle(r)` — each pattern creates local variables; use distinct names or reuse safely per arm
Putting the wrong number of fields in the pattern: `Rectangle(w)` won't compile — must match the definition's field count
Forgetting `0.5` for triangle area — `base * height` alone gives the area of a rectangle, not a triangle
